questions.prompt: A tall pea plant (Tt) is self-pollinated. What fraction of the F2 offspring is expected to be homozygous (either TT or tt)?
questions.explanation: The F2 genotypes are 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so TT and tt together make 2 out of 4, which is one half.

questions.prompt: In an F2 generation from Tt x Tt, one quarter of the plants are TT. What is the full genotype ratio TT : Tt : tt?
questions.explanation: Each parent gives T or t with equal chance, so the offspring are 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt.

questions.prompt: All F1 plants from a TT x tt cross are tall, yet some F2 plants are dwarf. What does this show about the dwarf trait in the F1 plants?

expected_answer.value: It was present in the F1 plants but not expressed

options: It was lost in F1 and re-created by mutation in F2
It was present in the F1 plants but not expressed
It blended with tallness to give medium-height plants
It was destroyed by the dominant tall trait
questions.explanation: F1 plants are Tt, so they carry the recessive allele hidden by the dominant one; it reappears when tt combinations form in F2.

questions.prompt: A pea plant has the alleles Tt and is tall. Which statement correctly names its genotype and phenotype?
questions.explanation: Genotype is the allele combination (Tt); phenotype is the visible trait (tall).

questions.prompt: A pea plant shows the dominant tall trait. Which genotype(s) could it have?
questions.explanation: One dominant allele is enough to give the tall phenotype, so both TT and Tt plants are tall.

questions.prompt: A dwarf pea plant (tt) is crossed with a tall plant (Tt). What percentage of the offspring is expected to be dwarf?
questions.explanation: The tall parent gives T or t equally, so half the offspring are Tt (tall) and half are tt (dwarf).

questions.prompt: Which pair of sex chromosomes is found in a normal human male?
questions.explanation: Males have the XY pair of sex chromosomes; females have XX.

questions.prompt: A boy inherits his Y chromosome from which parent?
questions.explanation: Only the father has a Y chromosome, so a boy must have received it from his father's sperm.

questions.prompt: Of the 23 pairs of chromosomes in a human body cell, how many pairs are autosomes (not sex chromosomes)?
questions.explanation: One of the 23 pairs is the pair of sex chromosomes, so the other 22 pairs are autosomes.

questions.prompt: Which part of the eye changes its curvature so that we can focus on objects at different distances?
questions.explanation: The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the lens, which changes its focal length.

questions.prompt: Which part of the eye carries the electrical signals produced on the retina to the brain?
questions.explanation: Light-sensitive cells on the retina generate signals that the optic nerve sends to the brain.

questions.prompt: When we step from a dark room into bright sunlight, the pupil becomes smaller. Why is this useful?

expected_answer.value: It reduces the amount of light entering and protects the retina

options: It makes the lens thicker for better focus
It reduces the amount of light entering and protects the retina
It lets more light reach the retina
questions.explanation: The iris contracts the pupil in bright light so that less light enters the eye.

questions.prompt: A student can read a book comfortably but cannot read the writing on the board from the last bench. Which defect does the student have and which lens corrects it?

expected_answer.value: Myopia, corrected by a concave lens

options: Myopia, corrected by a concave lens
Myopia, corrected by a convex lens
Hypermetropia, corrected by a concave lens
Hypermetropia, corrected by a convex lens
questions.explanation: Seeing near objects but not far ones is myopia, corrected by a diverging (concave) lens.

questions.prompt: In a hypermetropic eye, the image of a nearby object is formed:
questions.explanation: The eye cannot bend near-object rays enough, so they would meet beyond the retina.

questions.prompt: A convex lens of power +2.5 D is used to correct a vision defect. What is its focal length?
questions.explanation: f = 1/P = 1/2.5 m = 0.4 m = +40 cm; the positive sign shows a convex lens.

questions.prompt: White light passes through a rectangular glass slab, yet no spectrum is seen on the other side. Why?

expected_answer.value: The emerging colours travel parallel to each other and recombine to appear white

options: A glass slab does not refract light at all
Glass slabs absorb every colour except white
The emerging colours travel parallel to each other and recombine to appear white
Dispersion happens only in lenses, not in glass
questions.explanation: The slab's opposite faces are parallel, so the colours separated inside emerge as parallel rays that overlap into white light.

questions.prompt: We see the Sun a couple of minutes before it actually rises above the horizon. This is due to:
options: Dispersion of sunlight by a prism
Scattering of red light by dust
Reflection of sunlight from the clouds
questions.explanation: Light bends as it passes through air layers of changing density, so the Sun appears raised above its real position.

questions.prompt: In a primary rainbow, which colour appears at the outer top edge of the arc?
questions.explanation: Red light deviates least, so it appears along the outer (top) edge of the primary rainbow with violet on the inner edge.

questions.prompt: In the chain phytoplankton -> zooplankton -> small fish -> tuna, which organism is the secondary consumer?
questions.explanation: Phytoplankton are producers, zooplankton are primary consumers, and small fish eat them so they are secondary consumers.

questions.prompt: Producers in a food chain hold 20000 J of energy. By the 10 per cent law, how much energy reaches the fourth trophic level?
questions.explanation: Each step passes on 10 per cent: 20000 -> 2000 -> 200 -> 20 J at the fourth level.

questions.prompt: Which organisms break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil?
questions.explanation: Bacteria and fungi act as decomposers and recycle nutrients from dead matter.

questions.prompt: The thinning of the ozone layer, called the ozone hole, was first noticed over which region?
questions.explanation: Ozone depletion was first reported over Antarctica.

questions.prompt: Which pair contains only non-biodegradable items?
questions.explanation: Plastic and glass are not broken down by microbes, whereas paper, leaves and dung are.

questions.prompt: The build-up of harmful chemicals such as pesticides at successively higher trophic levels is called:
questions.explanation: These chemicals are not broken down, so their concentration increases at each higher level of a food chain.

questions.prompt: Na2SO4 + BaCl2 -> BaSO4 + 2NaCl, in which a white precipitate forms, is a:
questions.explanation: Two compounds exchange ions to form two new compounds, so it is double displacement.

questions.prompt: Fe + H2O -> Fe3O4 + H2 is balanced as 3Fe + xH2O -> Fe3O4 + yH2. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Fe3O4 has 4 oxygen atoms, so 4 H2O are needed, giving 4 H2 on the right.

questions.prompt: The pH of a solution falls from 4 to 2. How does its hydrogen ion concentration change?
questions.explanation: Each unit fall in pH means a tenfold rise in H+ ions, so two units means 100 times.

questions.prompt: H2SO4 reacts with NaOH in the ratio 1 : 2. What are the products?
questions.explanation: An acid and a base give a salt and water: H2SO4 + 2NaOH -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O.

questions.prompt: Cuscuta (amarbel) is a plant that lives on other plants and takes ready-made food from them. Its mode of nutrition is:
options: Autotrophic, as it is a plant
questions.explanation: Cuscuta lacks the ability to make its own food and absorbs it from its host, so it is a parasitic heterotroph.

questions.prompt: During very heavy exercise a muscle cell can run short of oxygen. What does it then form from pyruvate?
questions.explanation: In muscles, anaerobic breakdown of pyruvate gives lactic acid, which can cause cramps.

questions.prompt: Which of these non-metals is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite, a form of carbon, conducts electricity; most other non-metals (and diamond) do not.

questions.prompt: A piece of copper is placed separately in solutions of ZnSO4, FeSO4, AgNO3 and MgSO4. In which solution will a displacement reaction occur?
questions.explanation: Copper is more reactive than silver but less reactive than zinc, iron and magnesium, so it displaces only silver.

questions.prompt: How many electron pairs are shared between the two atoms in a nitrogen molecule (N2)?
questions.explanation: Each nitrogen needs three more electrons to complete its octet, so they share three pairs (a triple bond).

questions.prompt: Which pair of compounds belongs to the same homologous series?
questions.explanation: C3H8 and C5H12 are both alkanes (CnH2n+2) and differ by two CH2 units; the other pairs have different functional groups.

questions.prompt: An object is placed 45 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Where is the image formed?

expected_answer.value: 22.5 cm in front of the mirror

options: 22.5 cm in front of the mirror
11.25 cm in front of the mirror
30 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation: With f = -15 and u = -45, 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = -1/15 + 1/45 = -2/45, so v = -22.5 cm (real image in front).

questions.prompt: An object is 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. Find the image distance.
A 15 ohm resistor carries a current of 0.4 A. What is the potential difference across it?
Resistors of 6 ohm and 3 ohm are connected in parallel and this pair is joined in series with a 4 ohm resistor. What is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: The parallel pair gives 6 x 3 / (6 + 3) = 2 ohm; adding the 4 ohm in series gives 6 ohm.

questions.prompt: A long straight wire carries current vertically upward. Looking down from above, the magnetic field lines around it are:
options: Straight lines parallel to the wire
questions.explanation: Thumb along the current (up), the curled fingers show the field direction, which is anticlockwise when seen from above.

questions.prompt: In a reflex arc, which part carries the message from the spinal cord to the muscle?
questions.explanation: The motor neuron carries the response signal from the spinal cord to the effector (muscle).

questions.prompt: Which plant hormone is found in greater amounts in rapidly dividing tissues such as fruits and seeds?
questions.explanation: Cytokinins promote cell division and are abundant where cells divide rapidly.

questions.prompt: Which of these organisms reproduces by spore formation?
questions.explanation: Rhizopus produces spores; Amoeba divides by binary fission, Hydra by budding, and Planaria by regeneration.
